entries.reason: the protocol is carried by the classes of the port that answer for it; an application that holds an id of it gets an object of OpenGL ES 2.0 behind it
entries.effect: the protocol is there, and the methods of it the port does not do are not implemented; facts/Metal/Blits.md lists what a blit is done of and what it is refused for
entries.source: SDK 26.2, Metal; the behaviour is the one its header documents, and was not read from a shared cache

entries.reason: the command buffer of the port hands out the blit encoder of the port, the way it hands out the render command encoder; before this it answered nil and said in the log that a blit encoder had no form here
entries.effect: an object that copies between the buffers and textures of the port, or nil for a resource that is not one of the port's; facts/Metal/Blits.md is the whole of it
entries.source: SDK 26.2, Metal; the behaviour is the one its header documents, and was not read from a shared cache

entries.reason: a command is a call into OpenGL ES 2.0 that has already been made by the time it is encoded, so neither encoder of the port has a queue of work to flush: the blit encoder's copies are between CPU-resident buffers and textures, and the compute encoder's workgroup is one thread per thread of the group, joined by a mutex and a condition variable before the dispatch is encoded (facts/Metal/Compute.md). The member is declared by this protocol, which MTLBlitCommandEncoder, MTLRenderCommandEncoder and MTLComputeCommandEncoder all inherit, so it is named here once and not again per encoder.
entries.effect: the call returns, and the work it would have flushed has already been issued: for a blit the copy is done, and for a compute dispatch the threads have joined
entries.source: SDK 26.2, Metal; the behaviour is the one its header documents, and was not read from a shared cache

entries.reason: a debug group of the port is a name on a stack the encoder keeps, so that -popDebugGroup has one to pop and an unbalanced group can be seen
entries.effect: the name is pushed; the port does not print it, because the port's log is not a Metal capture
entries.source: SDK 26.2, Metal; the behaviour is the one its header documents, and was not read from a shared cache

entries.reason: a signpost is a string in a capture; the port has no capture to put it in
entries.effect: the call returns; a signpost changes no behaviour in Metal either, which is what its header says

entries.reason: a blit on this device is a copy on the CPU: a buffer of the port is its own bytes and a texture of it is an OpenGL ES 2.0 texture the port reads and writes a region at a time, so there is nothing to stage and nothing to transfer between
entries.effect: the copy is made, after the range has been checked against the resources it names; a copy the port cannot make writes one line in the log naming the reason and copies nothing, as facts/Metal/Blits.md lists
entries.source: SDK 26.2, Metal; the behaviour is the one its header documents, and was not read from a shared cache
